help_intro: A quick guide - pick a topic on the left.
help_workflow_body:
Click "Select & Translate" and drag over an area of the screen. Esc or right-click cancels.
The translation appears over the original text or in the toolbar's text panel - see "Direct overlay translation" in the "Interface" tab of Settings.
⟳ translates the same area again without selecting it anew - handy for subtitles and text that changes.
The overlay has buttons for copying and reading aloud.
Drag the toolbar by the empty space between the buttons; "—" minimizes it.
help_interface_body:
"Aa" - a window for translating typed or pasted text (button or Ctrl+Enter). With "Auto-translate" checked, it translates a second after you stop typing.
The clock - this session's translation history: show again, copy or read aloud any entry. It is not kept after the app closes. Bottom right: how many translations were made and how many came from the cache.
The eye hides/shows the text panel.
"?" - this help, "About" and "Check for updates": asks GitHub whether a newer version exists. Only when you ask - the app never checks on its own.
help_translation_body:
By default Overlingo translates offline, on this computer ("On this computer (offline)", free Argos Translate models).
The first time you translate between two languages it offers to download them - about 70 MB per language pair, once. Without a direct model, the translation goes through English.
You can also download them beforehand: "Translation" tab of Settings → "Download offline languages".
Online: "Google Translate (free)" needs no key; "DeepL (API key)" and "Microsoft Translator (API key)" need your own key in the "API key" field.
If the chosen service fails, Google is tried automatically; without internet, the downloaded offline languages are used.
Offline quality is decent, but below the online services.
More OCR languages: the "Download language" button in the same tab.
help_audio_body:
Choose who reads in the "Audio" tab of Settings; the speed (0.5x-2x) is set there too.
"On this computer (offline)" (the default) uses the voices installed in the operating system. The tab shows which voice will read the translation language.
No voice for the language on the computer? The online Microsoft Edge voice reads instead (internet needed).
Adding voices - Windows: Settings → Time & language → Speech, or the Narrator voices (restart Overlingo afterwards); macOS: Accessibility → Spoken Content; Linux: speech-dispatcher / espeak-ng.
"Microsoft Edge (online)" always uses the natural online voices - picked by the translation language, or chosen by you.
help_hotkey_body:
"Select & Translate" - Ctrl+Alt+T by default; "Translate again" - Ctrl+Alt+R.
Enable them in the "Hotkey" tab of Settings; the combination then also shows in the button's tooltip.
They work on Windows and on Linux under X11 (not under Wayland).

help_requirements_body:
Overlingo needs Tesseract OCR, installed separately on your system (it is not bundled with the app). If it is missing, a dialog with the exact instructions for your platform appears on startup.
In the "Translation" tab of Settings, set the OCR language (the language of the text on screen) and the target language (a two-letter code, e.g. BG, EN, DE).
The interface language is in the "Interface" tab.

help_appearance_body:
"Interface" tab of Settings: size and color of the translated text, and how transparent the overlay is.
"Preserve original font size" - the overlay text matches the size of the original; if it can't be measured, the size from Settings is used.
"Hide overlay panel" - the toolbar's text panel starts hidden (the eye shows it).
"Auto refresh" re-translates the last area every few seconds (interval in the same tab) - for text that keeps changing.
Already-translated text comes from the cache, without a new request to the service - useful with a paid key.
"Restore defaults" resets all settings; your API key is kept.
help_files_body:
Settings (settings.json), logs (app.log, crash.log) and the offline models (argos-models) are next to the program; on macOS - in ~/Library/Application Support/Overlingo.
Copy the "argos-models" folder when you move to a new version, so you don't download the models again.
Only one Overlingo runs at a time - starting it again brings the open one forward.
Something doesn't work or the app closes? Send app.log and crash.log with the problem description (GitHub → Issues).
settings.json holds your API key - don't share it.
